To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The career path of firms in R&D networks is strongly correlated with the number of their patents and the coreness of firms changes with the number of collaborations.
the coreness value is a good measure to quantify the position of a firm within the R&D network and that firms change their behavior in partner selection dependent on their position.
the selection of partners in R&D collaborations is driven by the career paths of firms, where the career path is determined by the coreness of the firms, i.e. the position of firms in an R&D network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how firms select their partners in R&D alliances.
the question how firms choose their partners for R&D alliances.
the evolution of R&D networks, and the selection of partners by firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
newcomers and incumbents are not selected by firms based on their network position but rather based on their performance, measured by the number of patents.
firms do not change their strategy, but their partners do, as newcomers are attracted to the network and incumbents are pushed to the periphery.
firms do not select their partners in a strategic way, but that the network structure itself forces firms to change their behavior when they reach their best possible network position.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed change in behavior is not a consequence of strategic considerations, but rather a natural result of the evolution of the network.
newcomers to a network tend to collaborate with other newcomers, and well integrated firms tend to collaborate with newcomers and firms from the peripheries of the network.
newcomers to a network choose partners of similar integration, and incumbents choose partners of high integration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of the R&D network is mainly driven by the dynamics of firms’ coreness values, and that the selection of partners is mainly driven by a firms’ network position, i.e. its coreness value.
the evolution of the R&D network is driven by the career paths of firms.
the evolution of a network can be explained by a simple rule: firms choose partners of a similar coreness value until they reach their optimal position in the network.
